subject: Eval recap: micro-POC proposal — embeddings & rerank (recall vs hyperscalers)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@northpoint.ai>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Eval recap: micro-POC proposal — embeddings & rerank (recall vs hyperscalers)

Hi Alicia / Tom —

Thanks again for the conversation earlier. Quick recap from our side plus a concrete micro-POC proposal so we can validate the retrieval + rerank tradeoffs you care about (recall@k, tail latency, and per-query cost). I captured the items we discussed and proposed next tests below.

Key objectives you mentioned:
- Improve recall@10 for deep domain Q&A (legal/clinical notes) vs your current vendor baseline
- Keep end-to-end retrieval + rerank median latency under ~120ms for interactive UI flows
- Understand cost sensitivity: vector dimension tradeoffs (256 vs 768) and cost per 100k queries

High-level micro-POC (3 weeks):
1) Dataset: your 10k doc sample (you mentioned upload link) + holdout queries (we'll use your 500 seed queries).
2) Baselines to run in parallel: Hyperscaler A (AWS Bedrock), Hyperscaler B (GCP Vertex AI), Current vendor X (your prod), Redwood hosted + Redwood Dedicated variant (quantized).
3) Metrics: recall@1/5/10, MRR, retrieval latency (cold/warm), full-stack p50/p95 latency (retrieval + rerank), and cost-per-query estimations at 100k and 1M QPS budgets.
4) Vector dims to test: 256, 512, 768 (we'll compute embedding cost delta).
5) Failure scenarios: cold KV-cache, model fallback (smaller model) and region failover to ensure graceful degradation.

Suggested immediate asks for you: please upload the 10k sample and a CSV of the 500 queries (or confirm we can use the shared Drive link). I attached a short proposal & timeline (benchmark-proposal-v1.pdf) and a sample doc export filename we expect (northpoint_sample_docs_10k.csv).

Next steps from Redwood: Diego will sketch the exact infra for the micro-POC and list the data access needs; Marcus will propose windows for an SE deep-dive next week.

If that looks good I'll send a calendar invite for the SE deep-dive and lock the POC timeline.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
(attachment: benchmark-proposal-v1.pdf, pdf)
(attachment: northpoint_sample_docs_10k.csv, csv)

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@northpoint.ai>

Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eval recap: micro-POC proposal — embeddings & rerank (recall vs hyperscalers)

Thanks Vanessa — this looks aligned. A few clarifying Qs from our side before we upload: 

1) For the hyperscaler baselines, can you confirm you will run exactly the same retrieval pipeline (same tokenizer, same index config) for a fair comparison, or do we need to provide config files?
2) For cost calc: please provide assumptions for embedding pricing per 1M vectors at 256 vs 768 dims. We want to compare both inference and storage costs.
3) Timeline: our legal wants a short MSA addendum for micro-POCs. Can the POC be executed under our standard evaluation SOW?

We'll upload the 10k CSV to the Drive by EOD Mon (link in my signature). For now I'm ok with the 3-week proposal but would like the first run (baseline numbers) within 5 business days of data upload.

—Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Search & Retrieval, Northpoint Labs
alicia.gomez@northpoint.ai
(Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bExampleUploadLink)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@northpoint.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2026 11:24:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Eval recap: micro-POC proposal — embeddings & rerank (recall vs hyperscalers)

Alicia — quick technical clarifications and what we'll log for apples-to-apples: 

- Retrieval pipeline: we'll replicate your current sparse index parameters if you provide them; otherwise we'll run a standard FAISS IVF-PQ setup with the same tokenization and stopword normalization. For hyperscalers, where we can't control internals, we'll match the preproc and use their recommended index configs.
- Embedding generation: Redwood will run the same model family across all runs where available (open-source equivalents) and a Redwood-optimized quantized variant for Dedicated. This reduces variance from differing model families.
- Caching: we'll report cold-start (no cache), warm-cache (after synthetic warm-up), and steady-state (continuous queries) latencies. We'll also report KV-cache hit rates for rerank if you use prefix caching in your UI flow.
- Cost assumptions (quick ballpark for proposal):
    * 256-d embeddings: $0.55 per 1M vectors (storage + compute amortized over runs)
    * 512-d embeddings: $1.10 per 1M vectors
    * 768-d embeddings: $1.65 per 1M vectors
  (we'll return a formal breakdown after first run; these are conservative estimates factoring in dedicated GPU amortization vs hosted API).

Tests we'll run and outputs:
- recall@1/5/10, MRR table per model+dim
- retrieval latency distribution (p50/p95/p99)
- full-stack p50/p95 for search -> rerank -> final score (ms)
- cost-per-100k-queries & extrapolated cost-per-1M with simple sensitivity to dims and model size

I'll prepare a README for the Drive folder with the exact command lines & index configs we'll use. If you can drop your sparse index config, that'd help ensure perfect parity.

Diego
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.com
(attachment: northpoint_index_config_example.json, json)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eval recap: micro-POC proposal — embeddings & rerank (recall vs hyperscalers)

Alicia — thanks for the fast turnaround. Confirming next steps and timeline: 

1) You upload 10k docs + 500 queries to the Drive by EOD Mon.
2) Diego will push the README + index config and kick off the first baseline run within 24 hrs of upload. Deliverable: baseline report (recall table + latency breakdown) within 5 business days of upload.
3) Week 2: Redwood runs hyperscaler comparisons and Dedicated quantized run; we’ll include cost pro-formas for 100k and 1M query budgets.
4) Week 3: Deep-dive session to review results and agree on production POC scope (rolling window tests, longer tail tests).

Scheduling: Marcus will propose 2 slots for the SE deep-dive (Wed/Thu next week). Please let us know preferred time zone.

Legal/Procurement: we'll put a short SOW addendum into HubSpot for signature (we've done this many times; minimal friction). I’ll loop in our contracts team only if you want non-standard terms.

A couple of Redwood differentiators to watch for in these tests (so you can flag them when you review results):
- Unified runtime that keeps the same API surface and tracing across Hosted/Dedicated/Private — makes apples-to-apples comparisons of latency and cost easier.
- Intelligent batching + prefix (KV) caching that often reduces per-query token cost without increasing tail latency.
- Quantized Dedicated runs that can push latency down and cost per query relative to standard hosted hyperscaler endpoints.

If that all sounds good I'll send the calendar invites and the short HubSpot SOW link.

Appreciate it,
Vanessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
